t: That from and after the approval of this Act, that portion of the Harney National Forest in the Black Hills of South Dakota heretofore known as the Custer State Park Game Sanctuary and adjoining or in the vicinity of the Custer State Park and the Mount Rushmore National Memorial reservation and referred to in the Act of June 5, 1920 (Public Law 258 of the Sixty-sixth Congress, 41 Stat. 986), as amended, and the Act of June 24, 1948 (Public Law 747 of the Eightieth Congress, 62 Stat. 580), shall be known and designated as the Norbeck Wildlife Preserve and that all records, surveys, maps, and public documents of the United States and of the State of South Dakota in which Custer State Park Game Sanctuary is referred to shall be held to refer to the Norbeck Wildlife Preserve.

fable.w: This section only renames the Custer State Park Game Sanctuary as the Norbeck Wildlife Preserve and directs that existing records be read to refer to the new name. The tempting reading is that the mention of the State of South Dakota and its documents signals state involvement, but the State is not consulted or given any role in a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: shall be known and designated as the Norbeck Wildlife Preserve

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely administrative renaming of a federal land area. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements for state/local input mentioned in the text.
qwen_block.s: That from and after the approval of this Act, that portion of the Harney National Forest in the Black Hills of South Dakota heretofore known as the Custer State Park Game Sanctuary... shall be known and designated as the Norbeck Wildlife Preserve

South Dakota is named only because its documents are covered by the renaming; it has no consultative or decision-making role. Nothing brings an outside party into a federal decision, so this is not participation.
opus.s: shall be known and designated as the Norbeck Wildlife Preserve and that all records, surveys, maps, and public documents of the United States and of the State of South Dakota in which Custer State Park Game Sanctuary is referred to shall be held to refer to the Norbeck Wildlife Preserve.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions the State of South Dakota and its public documents, which might look like federal-state coordination. That reading fails because the State has no role in any federal decision. The section only renames an area and says that existing federal and state records should be read to use the new name. There is no consultation, hearing, advisory body, comment period, rulemaking, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section solely mandates the renaming of a specific area within the Harney National Forest to the 'Norbeck Wildlife Preserve' and requires that records and documents reflect this new name. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) in making this decision. The actors involved are the federal government (via the Act) and the state of South Dakota (via its records), but the action is a unilateral legislative designation, not a participatory process.
